full_judgment: 6. From a plain reading of the section, we are of the opinion that in view of wide power given to the court by the expression, to summon any person as a witness or examine any person in attendance though not summoned as a witness, is inclusive of any person whose statement has been recorded by the investigation officer under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure during investigation as a witness but his name is not included in the list of witnesses in the column of charge-sheet. Broadly speaking, the court has unfettered discretion to call any person to be examined as a witness. It cannot be said that intention of this section is to limit its application to a person whose statement was recorded by the Investigating Officer under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and his name is included in the list of witnesses. The crucial test is, whether evidence of any person sought to be examined as a witnesses appears to the court essential to the just decision of the case or not. In the case of Hemayet Uddin Awronga vs State reported in 46 DLR (AD) 186 a report on which the learned Advocates of both sides placed their reliance, it is held that it cannot be said that the intention of the section is to limit it application to court witnesses only. If investigation officer submitted the application to include the names of two persons in the column of charge-sheeted witnesses upon misconception of law that unless name appears in the charge sheet as witness he cannot be called as witness. Be that as it may, question of further investigation of the case for including names of two witnesses as charge-sheet witnesses does not arise for the court has power to examine any person as a witness. The name of any person is included as witness in the charge-sheet or not is immaterial. The decision of Gujarat High Court is not applicable in the instant case.
